text.what: Chilling the crushed fruit and holding it below fermentation temperature for days before the yeast start. Water pulls colour and aroma out of the skins; alcohol has not arrived yet to pull tannin.
text.how: Three to six days near 10 °C, usually under dry ice or a blanket of CO₂ to keep spoilage organisms and oxygen out. Whether it does what its advocates claim is one of the livelier arguments in a pinot cellar.

kin.as: A decision taken at the same moment, on the same fruit.
Cold soak lasts until something starts the ferment — which is where this comes in.
